**Finding: COMPLIANT (preferred position met) — no redline proposed.**

Investigation summary:
- **Section 2 (Grant of Rights, p0030–p0045):** every licence to Corio is "nonexclusive" and runs in our favour. Section 2.4 actually restricts Commerce One (no direct non-ASP contact with Corio Customers; mandatory referral back to Corio) — exclusivity-flavoured protection *benefiting* Corio, which is not flagged.
- **Definitions (p0013, p0019, p0024):** CORIO MARKET SEGMENT and TERRITORY merely scope where/to whom the licences may be exercised; they contain no purchasing or sourcing commitment.
- **Section 13 (Shared Resources) and 13.6:** expressly preserves each party's right to develop independently — no field-of-use or non-compete restraint on Corio.
- **Exhibit D (p0197–p0205):** the only "lead with the product" style language, and it is expressly framed as "non-binding sales and marketing cooperation efforts" (cross-selling incentives, joint plans, marketing fund, two initial customer orders on a commercially-reasonable-efforts basis). Non-binding cooperation is not an exclusivity covenant.
- **Exhibit B (p0155–p0161):** revenue share is a fee mechanic, not a requirements commitment; no minimum volume or sole-source obligation.
- Targeted searches for "exclusive", "exclusively/solely from", "shall not sell/offer/procure", "all of its requirements", "competitor" returned only nonexclusive licence grants, tax language, "sole and exclusive remedies/owner" (Commerce One warranty) and the entire-agreement clause — none imposing exclusivity on us.

Preferred element "Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation" is already met on the face of the document, so we take no position and leave the clause set as drafted.
